claim: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(p,q\) be polyhedral norms on \(X\). Then \(p\) and \(q\) belong to the same intrinsic part of the cone \(\mathcal N(X)\cup\{0\}\) if and only if their triangular defects have the same zero set: \[\Delta_p(x,y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Delta_q(x,y)=0\qquad(x,y\in X).\] Equivalently, for polyhedral norms the triangle-equality relation alone determines intrinsic-part membership. In the nontrivial direction, equality of the zero sets forces constants \(a,b>0\) such that \(a\Delta_p\le\Delta_q\le b\Delta_p\) on \(X\times X\).
integrity: The proof uses a finite common polyhedral subdivision, an affine zero-set comparison lemma on each compact cell, positive homogeneity, and the published triangular-defect criterion. No numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: Finite-dimensional real polyhedral norms only; no exact intrinsic-distance formula is claimed. A closely related 2026 polyhedral-model preprint was inspectable only at abstract/metadata level, leaving a stated originality risk.
title: Polyhedral triangle-equality patterns determine intrinsic parts
